AMENDMENT (pre-grill, from the adversarial review of the idea set). Two changes:
(1) DECLARE THE DEPENDENCIES. AC-4 as written depends on 12/11's decisions read (which is itself amended and may move), and the AC-2 route depends on 12/12's composite gesture — neither dependency is declared anywhere. AMEND: name both, or drop AC-4's 12/11 half to a later slice.
(2) THE REFUSAL NAMES MUST BE THE ENGINE'S, NOT INVENTED. AC-5 tests 'the unknown-target refusal' and 'the empty-scope refusal' — those names belong to 12/12's validated gesture (AC-1), so this contract must consume the names 12/12 actually produces rather than asserting its own. AMEND: state that the e2e asserts the NAMED refusals from the engine route, whatever 12/12 fixes them as.

THE TRANSFER AFFORDANCE (12/13) — the door, and the four calls behind it.

D1 THE ROUTE (AC-2). POST /api/transfer as its own NAMED route, not a transfer{} key on /api/gate. The deciding reason: AC-2's own key list IS the body (id · gate · decision · transfer{target, scope} · why), and a gesture that names a successor and a scope deserves its own shape validation rather than widening a write every existing client already sends. It dispatches the SAME gate! composite — never a second write path — and the /api/gate precedent holds throughout: shape refusals are usage 400 (checked by NAME: an unknown key is refused with its own name), the engine's semantic refusal round-trips as its NAMED error at 500, and every refusal is ZERO writes.

D2 THE PICKER (AC-1/AC-3). The source is /api/packet's siblingStatus.siblings — the LEG's tasks, open and CLOSED alike (a closed node is a legal successor; the scope moves ONTO it), minus the node itself, so the engine's transfer-self refusal is unreachable from the page. The option's VALUE is the bare id and its LABEL carries the status. The client cannot type an id (it is a select) and the route refuses an unknown target regardless — the picker NARROWS, the route GUARDS. When the picker holds no real successor the button is disabled WITH the reason beside it, never a click the engine would refuse.

D3 THE BOUNDARY (AC-5). A transfer appears only where a decision is IN HAND, and the route enforces it: transfer-not-live at 409, read from the SAME confirm value the card reads (a confirm gate that is not submitted refuses). It lives in the ROUTE and not the engine because gate! deliberately AUTO-SUBMITS an undecided gate — delivered behaviour under review (12/12) that this route must not silently widen into 'move the scope past a review nobody made'. PROBED, not assumed: on a confirm gate with no submission the bare CLI accepts gate! … --transfer and writes submitted, confirmed, transferred. So the refusal is the route's, its message names the gesture that makes the same call legal (ann submit! <id> confirm, then move the scope), and the transfer-* family stays the engine's own.

D4 THE DRAFT (AC-3). spawn! is deliberately not a route, so a fresh successor is AUTHORED work. The card therefore DRAFTS instead of spawning: a button turns the scope box into a GENERATED contract (intent grounded on the moved criterion, acceptanceCriteria the criteria verbatim with the scope convention's id prefix stripped) plus the exact ann spawn! line to run, set under a GENERATED label ahead of the bytes. NOTHING LEAVES THE PAGE — no request, no spawn, proven by construction rather than by a guard. The draft follows the human's LAST edit, and its AC ids are the old task's — which is why it is a draft and not a mutation.

WITNESS. 5 new page tests in the drill suite (61 total) and 6 e2e over real HTTP: the happy path (one call lands the accept AND the move; the node then reads the successor named, the moved AC no longer an owed gap), the shape-by-name refusals, the unknown target, the empty scope (the route's 400 for a bare empty string, the engine's transfer-empty-scope for a whitespace-only one), and the boundary state. Each refusal is asserted BYTE-IDENTICAL on the node's own log, so 'zero writes' is a fact about the file and not a claim about the response.
